When the blood reaches the liver, hepatocytes take up the unconjugated bilirubin molecules. This is a hydrophobic molecule which is insoluble in water, so the liver makes a protein called glutathione S-transferase which conjugates 2 glucuronic acid molecules to the bilirubin. This makes the bilirubin much more water soluble and it is now conjugated bilirubin.  This is then passed into the bile canaliculi which drain into the common bile duct which joins the pancreatic duct. It then enters the second part of the duodenum through the hepatopancreatic sphincter (hepatoduodenal ligament).  The conjugated bilirubin reacts with bacteria in the intestine to form urobilinogen.  Most of the urobilinogen is oxidised to form the brown pigment stercobilin which gives faeces its characteristic colour.
